analysis.title: Canadian Pacific Kansas City Ltd. (CP.TO): 3Q26 EPS Light on Margins, Double-Digit EPS Growth Guide Reiterated for FY26
key_insights: CP (Neutral) reported 3Q26 adjusted core combined operating EPS of C$1.28 against C$1.31 for both GSe and Visible Alpha consensus, a miss of about 2.7%.
Adjusted core combined operating ratio was 61.9%, 80bps worse than the 61.1% consensus and 100bps worse than the 60.9% GSe. EBIT was about 3% below GSe on roughly in-line revenue.

The margin miss came mainly from higher salaries and fuel expense, partly offset by lower purchased transportation expense. CP cited higher stock-based compensation and wage inflation, partly offset by productivity.
Revenue matched GSe at C$4,219M vs C$4,224M. Revenue per carload rose about 10% YoY (in line with GSe) and carloads rose 5.2% YoY vs 4.8% forecast. Non-freight revenue was C$80M vs C$73M GSe.
Carload growth accelerated to +5.2% YoY in 3Q26 from roughly flat in 2Q26. Ex-intermodal carloads rose 3% (vs 1% in 2Q) and intermodal rose 9% (vs -1% in 2Q).
Early 4Q26 rail traffic data shows CP total carload growth still positive at about +4% YoY, tilted toward intermodal over ex-intermodal business.
Operating metrics in 3Q26: average train weight flat YoY, train length -1% YoY, train speed +8% YoY.
CP reiterated 2026 guidance of low-double-digit adjusted EPS growth and mid-single-digit revenue-ton-mile volume growth (unchanged). Headcount is expected to be down slightly in 2026.

GS leaves FY26/27/28 EPS essentially unchanged at C$5.07/C$5.90/C$6.65 (prior C$5.10/C$5.90/C$6.65). The 3Q miss is offset by a higher revenue trendline against a slightly lower margin trajectory, with 4Q26 held at C$1.50.
GS FY26 EPS growth is about 10% YoY, against management's low-double-digit guide and a prior GS estimate of about 11%.

Investor focus remains on KSU merger synergies. CP exited 2025 at about $1.2B annual synergy run-rate and expects $1.4-$1.5B by end of 2026. MMX180/181 cross-border Mexico-US intermodal service is cited as a continued source of support.
Management said further Class 1 rail consolidation is not necessary at this time, stressing that mergers must enhance competition, and pointed to the scale of a UNP/NSC merger.

GS raised the 12-month CP.TO price target to C$134 from C$132 (about 21.0x P/E on Q5-Q8 EPS of C$6.46) and the CP target to $97 from $96 at a 1.38 USD/CAD rate. Rating stays Neutral, and GS applies a premium multiple to the rail sector for synergy-driven growth.

market_movers.rationale: Neutral reiterated after a 3Q26 EPS and operating ratio miss. Target raised slightly to C$134 from C$132 on a rolled-forward EPS base, with estimates essentially unchanged.

sector_views.rationale: GS applies a premium multiple to CP versus the rail sector because KSU synergy gains are separate from the economy and from what other rails might earn.

earnings_insights: CP 3Q26 adjusted core combined operating EPS reported 10/28 was C$1.28 vs C$1.31 GSe and Visible Alpha consensus est, a miss of 2.7%.
3Q26 revenue reported C$4,219M vs C$4,224M GSe (-0.1%) and C$4,200M consensus est (+0.5%).
3Q26 EBIT reported C$1,608M vs C$1,653M GSe (-2.7%) and C$1,650M consensus est (-2.5%).
3Q26 recurring net income reported C$1,119M vs C$1,155M GSe and C$1,148M consensus est.

3Q26 adjusted core combined operating ratio reported 61.9% vs 60.9% GSe and 61.1% consensus est. Salaries and benefits were 16.8% of revenue vs 15.6% GSe, and fuel was 15.8% vs 15.4%. Purchased transportation was 13.4% vs 14.2% GSe.
3Q26 volume reported +5.2% YoY vs +4.8% GSe. Average revenue per unit reported +9.6% vs +10.3% GSe, and total revenue growth reported +14.8% vs +15.2% GSe.

Intermodal 3Q26 volume reported +8.6% YoY vs +9.0% GSe, with intermodal pricing +12.4% vs +15.0% GSe and revenue +20.9% vs +24.0% GSe. Grain revenue was +27.3% and potash pricing was +19.0% vs +14.0% GSe.
FY26/27/28 GS EPS estimates are C$5.07/C$5.90/C$6.65 (prior C$5.10/C$5.90/C$6.65). GS quarterly EPS estimates are 4Q26E C$1.50, 1Q27E C$1.21 and 2Q27E C$1.42.
2026 guidance reiterated: adjusted EPS growth of low-double-digits YoY against GSe and Street expectations of about +11% YoY going into the print.
risk_factors: Macro risk to volume recovery, tied in part to tariff implications.
Execution risk in combining the KSU and CP networks and falling short of synergy expectations.
Extended or renewed labor stoppages due to strikes.
Lower near-term spot trucking rates could make it harder to take immediate share, particularly if service does not keep improving.
Near-term cost pressure from wage inflation, stock-based compensation and fuel.

tension_points.bull_case: Solid volume and yield potential beyond 2026, with synergies at a $1.4-$1.5B run-rate by end of 2026 and cross-border intermodal growth. GS leaves estimates unchanged and credits an efficient railroad despite a tough fuel backdrop.
tension_points.bear_case: 3Q26 operating ratio was 61.9% vs 60.9% GSe on higher salaries and fuel, and near-term cost pressure is flagged. Risks include tariff-linked volume, weaker spot trucking rates and labor stoppages.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CP falls short of the $1.4-$1.5B synergy run-rate expected by the end of 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Synergy capture and volume and yield growth beyond 2026 support unchanged estimates despite the 3Q margin miss.
theme_stances.evidence: solid volume and yield potential beyond 2026
